column2: The coffers are left open and unattended again. Surely, this is [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s way of telling me that a small bonus is in order. [Root.Liege.GetSheHeCap] knows the other councilors would object if it were mentioned in their presence.

I've received a request for additional funds from my [Root.GetSpymasterName] [Root.job_spymaster.GetFirstName]. [Root.job_spymaster.GetSheHeCap] is worried that it is too easy for spies to make their way inside your home and wants to take precautionary measures against hostile operations.

Your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] approaches you with a request: 'My [Root.GetLordLady], I want your permission to travel to the heathen lands of the north and spread the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith among those benighted people. It shall be for the glory of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].'
Your zeal does you credit. [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] be with you.
Very well, if you insist.
No, I will not allow it.

My [Root.GetLordLady],

I would like us to invest in building a great temple for the glory of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]. I will contribute from my own purse to the construction costs.

Ever in service of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith,
[Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]
A great idea!
It would be a waste of money.
[Root.GetCouncilConvertDesc520]
[Root.GetCouncilConvertOptA520]
[Root.GetCouncilConvertDesc522]
[Root.GetCouncilConvertOptA522]
[Root.GetCouncilLettersDesc527]
[Root.GetCouncilLettersOptA527]
[Root.GetCouncilLettersOptB527]

Your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName], [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledNameWithNick], has been discovered charging money for various religious favors, putting the gold in [Root.job_spiritual.GetHerHis] own pocket.
Intolerable!
Disappointing, but understandable.

My [Root.GetTitle],
I find life here among the heathens both wretched and dangerous, and I am convinced that they are both blind and deaf to the glory of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]. I plead with you to allow me to return home where I can do more useful work for the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith.

Your loyal servant,
[Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledFirstName]
Very well, I will recall [Root.job_spiritual.GetHerHim].
The whining coward will be of no use there anyway.
[Root.job_spiritual.GetSheHeCap] must stay and do [Root.job_spiritual.GetHerHis] duty.

Your [Root.GetMarshalName], [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledName], has come to you with a suggestion: 'My [Root.GetLordLady], it is my opinion that [council_commander_pick.GetTitledNameWithNick] would make an excellent military commander. I suggest we make use of [council_commander_pick.GetHerHis] talents for the good of the realm.
Very well.
No, I have other candidates in mind.

Your [Root.GetMarshalName], [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledName], has put forward a plan for experimentation with new war machines, inspired by a supposedly brilliant engineer that [Root.job_marshal.GetSheHe] has recently befriended. The fellow claims to have studied at the Imperial Gunnery School of Nuln before a small misunderstanding about a crater. All that is needed is a little funding...
You shall have it.
No, this is pointless.
The Steam Wagon

You receive a report on the outcome of the military experiments that your [Root.GetMarshalName] asked you to sponsor. Apparently, a great steel-plated wagon was built around a hissing boiler, with a commander peering out from a turret on top and a cannon firing through a slit in the front. It was too slow, too thirsty and far too expensive to send to war, and it only exploded once. Still, the trials provided some valuable lessons.

You receive a report on the outcome of the military experiments that your [Root.GetMarshalName] asked you to sponsor. Apparently, a great steel-plated wagon was built around a hissing boiler, with a commander peering out from a turret on top and a cannon firing through a slit in the front. Unfortunately, its weight caused a wooden bridge to collapse and the contraption was lost in the river, where its boiler burst and killed the engineer. The [Root.GetMarshalName] [Root.job_marshal.GetHerselfHimself] barely escaped with [Root.job_marshal.GetHerHis] life.
I'm glad something came out of the investment.
Oh no!
Screaming Arrows

You receive a report on the outcome of the military experiments that your [Root.GetMarshalName] asked you to sponsor. Apparently, a battery of rockets was tried out, built after Cathayan models. Lit by fire, these rockets would scream and fly away leaving a trail of smoke and then explode on impact, killing several of the livestock used as practice targets. Though of dubious accuracy and prone to failure in rainy weather, these experiments have still provided some valuable lessons.

You receive a report on the outcome of the military experiments that your [Root.GetMarshalName] asked you to sponsor. Apparently, a battery of rockets was tried out, built after Cathayan models. Lit by fire, these rockets would scream and fly away leaving a trail of smoke and then explode on impact, killing several of the livestock used as practice targets. Unfortunately, on the second trial, several of them misfired, one striking the engineer dead and another nearly killing the [Root.GetMarshalName].
Trumpets of Doom

You receive a report on the outcome of the military experiments that your [Root.GetMarshalName] asked you to sponsor. Apparently, the experiments consisted in training a large force of musicians to blow their trumpets in unison, thus deafening and stunning the enemy army in preparation for an attack. Attempts were also made to shake castle walls to rubble by sheer noise alone.\n\nUnfortunately, while quite expensive, none of these experiments were successful.
Trumpets? How much did I pay for this again...?
Burning Sheep

You receive a report on the outcome of the military experiments that your [Root.GetMarshalName] asked you to sponsor. Apparently, the experiments consisted in drenching a large amount of sheep in oil and setting fire to them, then sending the terrified, screaming animals towards the enemy. Unfortunately, it proved impossible to control the direction of the sheep. The engineer was immolated in a ball of fire and your [Root.GetMarshalName] barely escaped with [Root.GetHerHis] life.
It seems we'll be dining roast mutton...

You receive news of your [Root.GetMarshalName]'s activities in [Root.job_marshal.Location.GetName]. It appears [Root.job_marshal.GetSheHe] has been spreading ill words about your rule, encouraging disloyalty among the peasantry!
A traitor cannot be [Root.GetMarshalName]!
Ill tidings, but I still need [Root.job_marshal.GetHerHim].

Worrying reports have reached you regarding your [Root.GetMarshalName], [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledFirstName]. It seems [Root.job_marshal.GetSheHe] has been using your soldiers to extort money from the peasantry in [Root.job_marshal.Location.GetName].
[Root.job_marshal.GetSheHeCap] has forfeited [Root.job_marshal.GetHerHis] office!
I will deal with this later.

I can't stand it any more! Every time we have a visitor from another realm in the court of the [From.GetTitle], [From.GetTitledFirstName] makes a fool of [From.GetHerselfHimself] trying to impress our visitors with [From.GetHerHis] non-existent knowledge of foreign languages.
I'll have to tutor [From.GetHerHim].
Hears my offer to tutor [From.GetHerHim].
This shouldn't bother me.

My [Root.GetChancellorName] [language_teacher.GetTitledFirstName] kindly suggests that it would be of benefit to the realm if I studied the languages spoken at foreign courts. [language_teacher.GetSheHeCap] also offers [language_teacher.GetHerselfHimself] to aid me in my studies.
An excellent idea!
If they can't speak [Root.Culture.GetName] they are not important.
Without the support of [language_teacher.GetTitledFirstName], your study sessions seem to be few and far between. You increasingly feel that the challenge is just too great to tackle on your own.
At least I made an effort.

Your determination and hard work has paid off. Studying with [language_teacher.GetTitledFirstName], you have learned several new languages to a decent level of fluency. This will surely increase your prestige at foreign courts!
I knew I could do it!

Distractions seem to overwhelm you during your studies. The simplest pleasures, and even plain and mundane chores, seem like time better spent than drowning in books all evening. How does one manage to keep focused when everything else is so much more appealing?
If I learn even a few phrases, it will be worth it!
I guess learning languages is not for everyone.
Language studies abandoned.

[Root.GetChancellorName] [language_teacher.GetTitledFirstName] has a look of parental disappointment in [language_teacher.GetHerHis] eyes. 'I believe you could have done this well if only you'd put your mind to it. Unfortunately your disinterest is all too apparent in your absence from our meetings. With your permission, I will henceforth focus on more useful work instead of waiting for you, my Liege.'
You will watch your tongue or lose it!
Although I learned less than expected, I thank you for your time.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] took offense at your offer of helping [From.GetHerHim] with [From.GetHerHis] language studies.
[From.GetHerHisCap] bad manners won't do [From.GetHerHim] any good.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] expressed [From.GetHerHis] gratitude for my offer to tutor [From.GetHerHim] in the languages of foreign courts. [From.GetFirstName] also commended me for the extra effort I put in for the sake of the realm.

While walking down the corridor a local peasant runs up to me with panic in his eyes: 'I came here to ask for aid since some of my sheep got killed by wild animals but now I just need to get out of here. I've already paid a dozen fees and been stuck in different rooms for hours in supposed 'queues' but I saw no-one else there. Please help my poor soul!'
Put [Root.job_chancellor.GetFirstName] in prison for [Root.job_chancellor.GetHerHis] bureaucratic scheme.
I'll let [Root.job_chancellor.GetFirstName]'s scheme slip by for now.

[target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] beams a smile at you while handing over a pouch of gold. [target_treasurer.GetSheHeCap] claims it contains the savings accumulated from hard work and donations from the richer families in your realm.
That's wonderful news!

A merchant approaches the court and carefully pleads to make a payment plan for the recent loan taken by [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName]. It seems the fruits of [target_treasurer.GetHerHis] labor may have been exaggerated, and since the loan was made in your name, this reflect poorly on you too. What will the consequence be for [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName]?
I will not tolerate incompetence!
We will have to make an example of [target_treasurer.GetHerHim].
Understandable, collecting taxes is tough work.

[target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] reminds you of all the good work [target_treasurer.GetSheHe] has done lately. [target_treasurer.GetSheHeCap] thinks that with a fair compensation from [target_treasurer.GetHerHis] own pocket the [requested_province.GetFullName] is only a modest request.
[target_treasurer.GetSheHeCap] is right, job well done.
[target_treasurer.GetSheHeCap] will be repaid, but not like this.
Are you blackmailing me? You'd be happy to keep your job!

[target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] approaches you: 'My liege, I have a great idea for a monument. Something to raise our cultural status and make the people notice what a great ruler you are. I would require some gold and your patience, and the work would take a year to complete.'
So be it! Surprise me!
I don't think so...

The monument [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] promised is finished. People have gathered to witness the unveiling of the new statue. It is a large portrait of [religious_head.GetTitledFirstName].
Surely, this will bring us the favour of the gods.

The monument [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] promised is finished. The shape of the statue seems a bit off, as it is unveiled some of the crowd seem confused. It is a giant ear with the inscription 'IT LISTENS'.
At least it's original.
Keep calm everyone! I am a snake!

The monument [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] promised is finished. The statue is unveiled and it's just a bigger version of [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName], only slightly better looking than the real [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName].
I don't know about this.
Tear it down! [target_treasurer.GetSheHeCap] will be put in [target_treasurer.GetHerHis] place.

The monument promised by [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] is finished. Some people in the crowd cover their children's eyes as the statue is unveiled. It's a couple in the middle of lovemaking, and not exactly presented in a tasteful way.
Children must learn this sooner or later.
Tear it down!

The monument promised by [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] is finished. At the unveiling, the crowd gasps and some even scream. It's something that resembles a throne, with an eyeless horned creature on top. It smells like blood.
I should have seen this coming.
The monument promised by [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] is finished. Upon unveiling, a statue of yourself is revealed and you notice the crowd smiling and giving you a round of applause.
I have no words.
It's too much, remove it.

[steward.GetTitledFirstName] smiles at you. 'My liege, I have noticed your mind seems to drift off whenever we discuss monetary issues. I believe that to make things interesting, one must be introduced to the subject where it is directly relevant to oneself. Perhaps you would like to join me tomorrow on a full days work?'
Yes, that would be interesting.
Hah! You must be joking, I have better things to do.

[steward.GetTitledFirstName] starts the day off collecting taxes. Some people frown and complain when they give away their earnings. [steward.GetTitledFirstName] calmly explains why taxes are collected and manages to appease the complainers.
Earning trust is earning gold.
Maybe we could squeeze them for some more?

Today, [steward.GetTitledFirstName] brings you to the nearest construction site to evaluate progress. [steward.GetTitledFirstName] notices that the builders are lagging behind the agreed schedule and proceeds to question them. The builders complain about the weather and want more pay to cover the delays. [steward.GetTitledFirstName] looks over your way, awaiting a response.
We will hold our end of the deal when you hold yours.
I guess one cannot predict the weather.
Clear the site! You will never work again!

A friend has come to visit [steward.GetTitledFirstName] this evening. The three of you have a good time discussing your experiences over a fine evening meal. The visitor nods at you, saying: 'How lucky you are, [steward.GetFirstName], to have a liege that understands your work. This cooperation should benefit the both of you.'
It's been interesting, moreso than many other things I've tried.
It wasn't for me, it feels like stealing.
I hated it! We should just kill the peasants and take their money.

Being a Council Member is a powerful, almost intimidating feeling. The authority, the impact of your decisions across the realm. Inside the circle of trust, so close to this unreal amount of money, one wonders - if some of the gold were to disappear, would anyone even notice?
I can take some, I deserve it.
No, it's not right.
Curious, I was as pleased as always when I saw the amount of coin in the coffers this morning. But looking at it now, the amount seems somehow... less. Could it be that someone is stealing from me?

Going through the treasury to account for today's earnings, it seems to me that the coffers seem to contain less than what we started out with today. Either someone is stealing my gold or I must be going mad.
When I catch the thieving little rat...
First they take my gold, and then what?

As you pass by the treasury, you stumble upon [From.GetTitledFirstName] digging through the coffers. You must have been quiet as [From.GetSheHe] looks very surprised. So this is where the missing gold has gone.

You close the door to your chamber, and as you approach your personal gold coffer you spot someone hiding behind it. A well aimed kick makes [From.GetTitledFirstName] squirm and the sound of what may be broken ribs accompanies [From.GetHerHis] scream of agony.
Let [From.GetHerHim] go in exchange for a favor.
This behavior is unacceptable.
Make [From.GetHerHim] swear to never do it again.

Your [Root.GetTreasurerName] [Root.job_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] has also noticed that coins are missing but has concluded that your [From.GetJobTitle], [From.GetTitledFirstName] is the only one that could've stolen it.
Remove [From.GetHerHim] from the Council.

I have been caught stealing from the coffers of my Liege. But [From.GetSheHe] has been kind enough to let me go with a warning. [From.GetSheHeCap] insists that I owe [From.GetHerHim] a favor, however.
That's fortunate.
I was caught stealing from the coffers, but was fortunate enough to be let go with a warning.
It could have been worse.

[blackmailed_target.GetTitledFirstName] has brought up a grave problem [blackmailed_target.GetSheHe] has with your [GetSpymasterName] [Root.job_spymaster.GetFirstName]. [job_spymaster.GetFirstName] has been using the realm's spies to go snooping about in the personal quarters of [blackmailed_target.GetFirstName] for [job_spymaster.GetHerHis] own personal gain.
Remove [Root.job_spymaster.GetFirstName] from the Council.
Remind [Root.job_spymaster.GetFirstName] to act in the shadows but take no direct actions.
Imply that I know secrets...
It can't hurt to be a little safer.
Start to plan defences.
It's too expensive.

Earlier today, my [Root.GetSpymasterName] [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] presented [safety_measure_spymaster.GetHerHis] plan to catch any sneaky spies at court. [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHeCap] has weakened the floorboards in strategic places to make sure a creaking noise is always heard when someone moves around during the night.

[safety_measure_spymaster.GetTitledFirstName] is trying out [safety_measure_spymaster.GetHerHis] new plan to get rid of intruders. [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHeCap] has been splashing soap on all of the floors to make it more hazardous to move around.
Now if only I could get rid of this terrible headache.
This is dangerous!

As I entered the gates I was greeted by a large barking dog. My horse was frightened and started to rear. I was just about to draw my blade to slay the beast when I saw my [Root.GetSpymasterName], [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName], come running, shouting: "Bad dog! This is our friend that we're supposed to protect." The dog then stopped barking and rolled around placidly on its back.

There's litter and feathers all over the place and when you enter the dining hall you see a huge pelican standing on the table. When [Root.GetSpymasterName] [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] sees my steaming face [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHe] tries to calm me down, introducing me to the new 'Pelican Guard'.
Good dog!
It bit me! Get rid of it!
It bit my sister! Get rid of it!

[GetSpymasterName] [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] presents a strange concoction to me. [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHeCap] places a peg on my nose and forces me to drink the vile concoction while mumbling something that this will help keep away the forces that lurk in the shadows.
Eugh! My mouth reeks of garlic.

When I walk into the office of my [Root.GetSpymasterName] [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] I find [safety_measure_spymaster.GetHerHim] carving huge and sharp stakes which [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHe] tells me will help bring down any intruder that dares to trespass. The enthusiastic smile on [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName]'s face gives me an eerie feeling.
If it keeps us safe...
This nonsense has to stop!

[safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] told me [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHe] had something exciting to show me. I was left unimpressed when it turned out to be a vial of ordinary water. [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] then told me that this 'blessed water' can drive away our enemies. The small donation demanded by the supplier had apparently already been taken care of.
Expensive water.
A great initiative!
This nonsense has to stop!

I heard shouting down the corridor and when I came around the corner I see [spiritual.GetTitledFirstName] loudly arguing with my [Root.GetSpymasterName] [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName]. Clearly outraged, [spiritual.GetFirstName] explained to me that [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] tried to convince [spiritual.GetHerHim] to declare the entire building sacred ground.
Enough of this!
[safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHeCap] was just joking. I hope you understand.
Surely, for the correct sum this can be arranged?

A dour Dawi reckoner of another clan has arrived at your hold with a ledger bound in iron. [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] borrowed a great sum in your name, and the 'savings' [target_treasurer.GetSheHe] boasted of were nothing of the sort. The reckoner wants the terms of repayment settled, and he has already written your name in a book that the Dawi do not forget. What will the consequence be for [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName]?

A big Goblin wiv a sack, a ledger he can't read and a dozen ladz wiv clubs has turned up at the gate. Seems [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] borrowed a heap of teef in your name and the 'savings' were nuffin' of the sort. The Goblin wants his teef back, wiv extra, or he starts takin' 'em out of mouths. What will the consequence be for [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName]?

A hooded Skaven of some merchant-clan scurries into your burrow, clutching a scroll of debts sealed with warpstone wax. [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName] borrowed warp-tokens in your name, and the 'savings' were a lie, yes-yes. The merchant names a payment plan with much bowing and much interest. What will the consequence be for [target_treasurer.GetTitledFirstName]?
Owes the Moneylenders
A loan taken in this ruler's name is being paid off, with interest, out of the realm's taxes.

Your [Root.GetMarshalName], [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledName], has brought a twitching Warlock Engineer of Clan Skryre before you. The creature promises war machines of terrible power, warp-driven and quite safe, yes-yes, mostly safe. All it needs is a little warpstone and a little gold, and nobody standing too close...

Your [Root.GetMarshalName], [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledName], has befriended a young engineer whose ideas are far too new for the Engineers Guild. The greybeards would call it reckless, and the Guild would never approve it, but the lad swears his designs will work. All that is needed is a little funding, and a little discretion...

Your [Root.GetMarshalName], [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledName], has dragged in a Goblin wiv singed eyebrows and a head full of big ideas. The git says he can build war machines that'll make the enemy wet 'emselves, and only a few of the ladz will get squashed testin' 'em. All he needs is a sack of teef...
Refused to Preach Among the Heathens
This character, while a [GetLordSpiritualName], refused to preach in heathen realms, deeming it much too dangerous.
At last, a monument worthy of the Dark Gods!

[GetSpymasterName] [safety_measure_spymaster.GetFirstName] presents a strange concoction to me, mumbling that it will keep away the forces that lurk in the shadows. Before anyone can stop [safety_measure_spymaster.GetHerHim], [safety_measure_spymaster.GetSheHe] pinches my nose and pours it down my throat. Garlic. A great deal of garlic. My insides burn like a pyre, and the madman stands there beaming, waiting to be thanked.
Get that lunatic out of my sight before I drain [safety_measure_spymaster.GetHerHim] dry!

The gods have sent an omen, or a joke. One of your courtiers has turned from the Dark Gods to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith, and prays to it openly, as if the eyes of the gods were not upon this court!
Oi! One of da gitz at court 'as gone an' started prayin' to da [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods instead of Gork an' Mork. Da ladz fink 'e's gone soft in da 'ead.
One of da gitz at court 'as started sneakin' off to pray to da [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods! Da uvver gobbos are whisperin' about it.
Strange-strange news! A courtier no longer squeaks to the Horned One but to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. Treachery? Madness? Both-both?
One of the hangers-on at your camp has stopped feeding the Great Maw and prays to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods instead. The tribe is talking about it over the cook-fires.
The temple-scribes report something unheard of. One of the court has turned from the Great Plan and now follows the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith.
The priestesses bring word that one of the court has left the shrines and now follows the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith.
It shames the hold to say it, but one of your courtiers has turned from the Ancestor Gods to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith! The elders are muttering into their beards.
One of your courtiers has turned from the Father of Darkness to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. The priests of Hashut are already sharpening their knives.
Strange news reaches the court. One of your courtiers has turned from the old gods of our people to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith.
One of your courtiers has turned from the temple to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. The Hag Sorceresses say the blood was always weak in that one.
Well, I never! One of the folk at court has stopped saying grace to Esmeralda and goes off to pray to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods instead.
Even the dead have noticed. One of your courtiers has turned from the true faith to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith.
Strange news reach your ears. Apparently, one of your courtiers has converted to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith!
Which god is laughing at me?
Wot's got inta 'im?
Wot's dat git playin' at?
Who-who is behind this?
Has someone been feeding them strange meat?
This was not in the Plan.
Who has led them astray?
Write it in the Book. Someone is behind this.
Hashut will want an explanation.
Why would anyone turn from the gods of our people?
Who has been whispering in their ear?
Whatever for?
The dead do not forgive.
Why in the name of the gods...?
Another courtier has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. The Dark Gods are either amused or furious, and neither bodes well for this court.
Anuvva git at court's gone over to da [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods! Somefin's fishy 'ere.
Anuvva git's gone sneakin' off to da [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods! Somefin' sneaky's goin' on, an' it ain't us.
Another! Another courtier squeaks to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith! Plots-plots, everywhere!
Another one has stopped feeding the Maw and prays to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods. Something smells wrong in this camp.
Another of the court has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. A pattern is forming, and it is not ours.
Another of the court has left the shrines for the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith.
Another courtier has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith! This is no accident. Someone is working at the roots of the hold.
Another courtier has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. The furnaces will have work soon.
Another of your courtiers has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. This is no chance.
Another courtier has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. Someone at court is spreading weakness like a plague.
Another one gone over to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] gods! Something odd is going on in this house.
Another of your courtiers has turned to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith. Something stirs against you.
It seems another of your courtiers has converted to the [council_mission_province.Religion.GetName] faith!
Someone is playing a game with me.
Sumone's bein' kunnin'. I'll find 'im.
Sumone's bein' sneakier dan me!
Find the traitor. Find-find!
I will find who did this and eat them.
The cause will be found.
Someone is behind this.
This is no accident.
Someone is behind this.
Someone is behind this.
I will find the traitor.
Something fishy is going on.
I will find the one behind this.
Something strange is going on here...

Letters have been found, written by your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName]. They praise the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith and mock the Dark Gods as tired old masters. Your own spiritual guide has been sowing heresy at your court!

Da ladz found a pile of letters from yer [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], sayin' da [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] gods are better dan Gork an' Mork! Dat's why da gitz went funny!

We found letters from yer [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], sayin' da [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] gods are better dan ours! Dat sneaky git's been at it all along!

Letters! Secret-secret letters from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], squeaking praise of the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith and spitting on the Horned One! The traitor is found!

Letters were found, scratched by your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], saying the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] gods fill the belly better than the Great Maw. That is why the camp went strange.

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith over the Great Plan. The cause of the heresy is known.
Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith over the shrines of the jungle.

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith and calling the Ancestor Gods old and tired. A grudge if ever there was one!

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith over the Father of Darkness. Hashut's priests demand a bull be heated.

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the simple virtues of the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith and mocking the gods of our people as tired and decadent. The source of the heresy is found.

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith and calling the temple's rites cruel and empty. The traitor is found.

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], going on about how the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] gods are better than Esmeralda. The cheek of it!

Letters have been found from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], praising the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName] faith and mocking the true lords of death. The source of the heresy is found.

A number of incriminating letters have been found. They are from your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetTitledName], addressed to various members of your court, praising the simple virtues of the [Root.job_spiritual.Location.Religion.GetName]s and contrasting them with the tired, decadent ways of the [Root.Religion.GetName]s. This surely explains the recent outbreak of vile flirting with heathenry at your court!
The gods will have their due from this traitor.
Get 'im! Krump da traitor!
Stab 'im! Stab da traitor!
Kill-kill the traitor!
Into the pot with the traitor!
The traitor will be removed.
The traitor will answer for this.
Into the Book with the traitor!
Into the bull with the traitor!
The traitor will be cast out.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] will have the traitor's heart.
Out of my house, you rotter!
The traitor joins the dead.
The heathen-loving traitor!
If this stops now, the gods may spare [Root.job_spiritual.GetHerHim].
Stop it now an' I won't krump ya. Dis time.
Stop it now an' I won't stab ya. Probly.
Stop-stop now, and live. For now-now.
Stop now and I will not eat you.
If it stops now, there will be mercy.
If this stops now, I shall forgive.
Stop now, and the grudge stays unwritten.
Stop now, and the bull stays cold.
If this madness stops now, I shall forgive.
Stop now, and keep your heart.
Stop it now and we'll say no more about it.
Stop now, and remain among the living.
If this madness stops now, I shall forgive.

Your chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] begs a word. "My [Root.GetLordLady], you hold more land than any one ruler can govern well, and the newer titles will rot while you see to the old. Let me find worthy hands for them, as befits your dignity."

Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been going over the ledgers. "My [Root.GetLordLady], half these holdings are run by nobody at all, and the taxes show it. Let me find capable vassals to take them off your hands."

[From.GetTitledFirstName] comes to you after the evening rites. "The gods do not smile on a lord who hoards more than [Root.GetSheHe] can tend. Let me see to it that your newer titles find worthy keepers."
Yes, I would appreciate some help!
No thanks, I can manage.
Stop bothering me about this nonsense!
None of your councillors will bother you about this for two years.
My liege has agreed to let me hand out [From.GetHerHis] recently acquired titles.
I will choose well.
My liege has refused to let me hand out [From.GetHerHis] recently acquired titles.
As my liege wishes.
My liege has given me one of [Root.Liege.GetHerHis] titles to hand out. Who shall have it?
The best candidate.
The second best candidate.
The third best candidate.
A noble from outside the court.
Someone close to me. Myself, in fact.

A woman named [From.GetFirstName] has come to court with letters of introduction from half the noble houses of the realm. She speaks three tongues, knows every envoy by name and every grudge between their masters, and she makes no secret of it: she wants my chancellor's seat, and she believes she would fill it better than the man who holds it now.
Then let us see what you can do. The seat is yours.
A woman at my council table? Show her the door.

[From.GetFirstName] rode into my courtyard at the head of a band of hard-bitten sellswords who obey her every word. She has fought greenskins in the passes and beastmen in the forests, and the scars to prove it. She tells me plainly that my marshal is a fool, and that she would make a far better one.
Bold words. Take the marshal's baton and prove them.
My armies will not follow a woman. Send her away.

[From.GetFirstName], the widow of a wealthy merchant, has come to court with her late husband's ledgers under her arm. In ten years she has doubled his fortune, and she has found three errors in my steward's accounts in a single afternoon. She would like his seat.
Anyone who can count like that has a place at my table.
My coffers are no business of a merchant's widow.

A woman called [From.GetFirstName] was found in my private chambers this morning, though no guard admits to letting her pass. She knew what I ate last night, whom I wrote to last week, and which of my courtiers takes coin from my rivals. She offers to put what she knows to my use, as my spymaster.
Better at my side than in a rival's pay. You have the seat.
Get rid of her. Quietly.

My [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has asked to speak with me alone. She knows the laws and the courts of the realm better than most of the men who sit on my council, and she asks me for the chancellor's seat.

My [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has asked to speak with me alone. She has studied every campaign of our house and knows more of war than many of my captains, and she asks me for the marshal's baton.
My [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has asked to speak with me alone. She has kept the household accounts for years without a single coin going astray, and she asks me for the steward's seat.
My [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has asked to speak with me alone. Little that is whispered at court escapes her, and she asks me for the spymaster's seat.
You have earned it. The seat is yours.
I cannot. The council is no place for you.
I hold my lands as well as any lord of the realm, and better than most. Yet when my liege's council meets, I am not in the room. That should change, and I know which seat I would take.
I will ask to be chancellor.
Ask your liege for the chancellor's seat.
I will ask to be marshal.
Ask your liege for the marshal's seat.
I will ask to be steward.
Ask your liege for the steward's seat.
I will ask to be spymaster.
Ask your liege for the spymaster's seat.
On second thought, my lands need me more.
You will not ask, and you lose your ambition.
[From.GetTitledName], one of my vassals, has asked for a seat on my council as chancellor. She is as skilled a diplomat as any man in my service.
[From.GetTitledName], one of my vassals, has asked for a seat on my council as marshal. She has led her own levies well, and knows it.
[From.GetTitledName], one of my vassals, has asked for a seat on my council as steward. Her own lands are the best kept in the realm.
[From.GetTitledName], one of my vassals, has asked for a seat on my council as spymaster. She seems to know a great deal about my other vassals.
[From.GetTitledName] has granted me the seat I asked for. My place is at the council table now.
As it should be.
[From.GetTitledName] has refused me a seat on the council. I will not forget it.
So be it.

Envoys leave my hall pleased these days, and merchants and lords alike speak well of my court. My chancellor, [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName], has spent years trading letters, favours and flattery on my behalf, and it has begun to pay. The burghers of my towns and the knights of my castles both send their thanks. I may reward one of them for their goodwill.
Feast the burghers and guildmasters.
Feast the knights and castellans.

My soldiers march in step, drill without grumbling and keep their weapons oiled. Marshal [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has made something of them. The sergeants swear by the marshal's name, and young men come from the villages to take the colours.
Let the troops toast their marshal.
Raise new companies where the marshal recruits.

My coffers are thin and the peasants mutter, yet [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has a plan. My steward has gone over every ledger, every toll and every tithe barn, and found coin where none was thought to be. The steward can wring more from the land or ease the burden on it. Not both.
Fill the treasury.
Ease the peasants' burden.

Spymaster [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has spun a web of informers through my realm: tavern keepers, laundresses, ferrymen and a few priests who should know better. Nothing moves in my lands without a whisper reaching the spymaster. The question is what to do with all these whispers.
Hunt down the plotters.
Use the whispers for my own schemes.

The faithful of my realm crowd the temples, and the priests sing my praises from the pulpits. [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has spent years preaching, teaching and visiting every shrine in my lands, and the clergy love my Lord Spiritual for it. Their goodwill could be mine as well.
Endow the temples.
Join the faithful at prayer.

I have watched [council_lustful_chancellor.GetTitledFirstName], chancellor to [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], hovering around my spouse [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName] at every feast. The flowers, the poems, the whispered jokes at table: it is all too plain, and the whole court is laughing behind its hands. I could take my complaint to our liege, or I could swallow my pride and hope it passes.
Our liege will hear of this!
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears your complaint.
Better to say nothing.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come to me, red-faced and shaking, with a complaint against my chancellor. [council_lustful_chancellor.GetTitledFirstName] is said to be pursuing [From.GetFirstName]'s spouse [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName] in my own hall, and making no secret of it. My chancellor is no fool and useful to me, but the court is talking.
Into the dungeon with the chancellor!
A sharp word in private will do.
The chancellor is too useful. Go home.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has listened to me and thrown [council_lustful_chancellor.GetTitledFirstName] into the dungeon. Let the chancellor write poems to the rats.
Justice is done.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has had me thrown in the dungeon over a few compliments paid to [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName]. Compliments! All for some jealous lordling's wounded pride.
This is an outrage!

That jealous fool [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName]'s spouse complained about me to [From.GetTitledFirstName], but our liege has sent them home with nothing. It seems I am worth more than a lordling's hurt feelings.
I am grateful, my liege.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has dismissed my complaint. The chancellor may keep sniffing around [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName], and I am to keep quiet about it. So this is what loyalty earns.
I will remember this.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] took me aside after the feast and told me, in words I will not soon forget, to keep away from [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName]. Our liege did not raise a voice once, which made it worse.
As you command, my liege.

Word has it [From.GetTitledFirstName] gave [council_lustful_chancellor.GetTitledFirstName] a dressing-down that left the chancellor white as chalk. I have not seen the chancellor near [council_courted_spouse.GetFirstName] since.
Good.
Not everyone at [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s court is content, and a good chancellor mends what is frayed before it tears. I have time and a quiet word to spare. Where should I spend them?
Win over [council_soothed_vassal.GetTitledFirstName].
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears of your work.
[council_soothed_vassal.GetTitledFirstName] warms to [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName].
Mend things between [Root.Liege.GetFirstName] and [council_soothed_spouse.GetFirstName].
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears of your work.
[council_soothed_spouse.GetFirstName] warms to [Root.Liege.GetFirstName].
Charm the whole court.
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears of your work.

[council_soothed_vassal.GetTitledFirstName] has been sulking for months, but my chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has spent many evenings with them over wine and old grievances. Now [council_soothed_vassal.GetFirstName] speaks of me kindly again.
Such diligence deserves a reward.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] is rewarded.
It is only the chancellor's duty.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] feels unappreciated.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has spent many evenings with me, listening to my grievances and explaining what [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] truly intended. Perhaps I have judged our liege too harshly.
Perhaps I have.

Things have been cold between [council_soothed_spouse.GetFirstName] and me, but my chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been carrying gentle words back and forth, arranging a walk in the gardens here and a shared supper there. [council_soothed_spouse.GetFirstName] smiled at me this morning.
Such diligence deserves a reward.
It is only the chancellor's duty.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has spoken to me at length about [From.Liege.GetFirstName], about the burdens of rule and the cares that make a ruler cold. Perhaps I have been unfair.
I will try again.

My chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been everywhere these past weeks: settling quarrels over seating, flattering old knights, finding husbands for hopeful maids. My court has seldom been in such good spirits.
Such diligence deserves a reward.
It is only the chancellor's duty.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has noticed my hard work and sent me a purse of gold with thanks.
Most generous.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] took all the credit for my work and did not so much as thank me. Why do I bother?
Why indeed?

The letters pile up on my desk, the envoys wait in the antechamber, and I cannot bring myself to care. Let them wait another day. Or a week. Sooner or later [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] will notice.
Tomorrow. I will see to it tomorrow.
Envoys have waited weeks for an answer, and a letter from a neighbouring court was found unopened under a wine jug. My chancellor [From.GetTitledFirstName] has done nothing at all for months.
Time for a stern talk.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] is taken to task.
Can it truly matter so much?
[From.GetTitledFirstName] keeps idling.
This is worth a cell!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has called me in and given me a talking-to I did not deserve. I am the chancellor, not some clerk to be scolded.
How dare [From.GetSheHe]!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] hears of your anger.
[From.GetSheHe] is right. I will do better.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has noticed my idleness and does not seem to care. Splendid.
Back to my nap.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has thrown me in the dungeon for neglecting my duties. Now I have nothing at all to do.
Unfair!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has taken my rebuke badly and sulks in the corridors, muttering about ingratitude.
Let the chancellor sulk.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has taken my words to heart. The letters are answered, the envoys received, and the chancellor's lamp burns late into the night.
Good.

[target_infidel.GetTitledName] walks freely at [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s court, an unbeliever who bows to [target_infidel.Religion.GetName]. Every day the infidel is tolerated is an insult to the gods. It falls to me, as Lord Spiritual, to see this put right.
The infidel must burn!
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears your demand that [target_infidel.GetFirstName] be burned.
Cast the infidel out of the realm!
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears your demand that [target_infidel.GetFirstName] be banished.
I will preach to this lost soul myself.

My Lord Spiritual, [From.GetTitledFirstName], stands before me with eyes burning. [From.GetSheHe] demands that [target_infidel.GetTitledName], who follows [target_infidel.Religion.GetName], be burned at the stake for the good of the realm and the glory of the gods.
Build the pyre.
I will not burn a guest of my court.
My Lord Spiritual, [From.GetTitledFirstName], demands that [target_infidel.GetTitledName], who follows [target_infidel.Religion.GetName], be cast out of my court and my realm.
Let the infidel go, and never return.
No. [target_infidel.GetFirstName] stays.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] heeded me. The infidel [target_infidel.GetFirstName] burned in the square while the faithful sang hymns.
The gods are honoured.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] refused me. The infidel [target_infidel.GetFirstName] still walks the halls, smiling at me.
The gods will judge us all.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] heeded me. The infidel [target_infidel.GetFirstName] has been driven from the realm with nothing but the clothes on their back.
Good riddance.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] refused me. The infidel [target_infidel.GetFirstName] remains at court.
The gods will judge us all.

[target_heretic.GetTitledName] calls [target_heretic.GetHerselfHimself] faithful, yet spreads the twisted teachings of [target_heretic.Religion.GetName] at [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s court. A heretic is worse than any infidel, for the rot comes from within. I am Lord Spiritual, and I will not let it spread.
The heretic must burn!
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears your demand that [target_heretic.GetFirstName] be burned.
Cast the heretic out of the realm!
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears your demand that [target_heretic.GetFirstName] be banished.
I will bring this stray back to the true faith.

My Lord Spiritual, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has come to me with a list of [target_heretic.GetTitledName]'s heresies as long as my arm. [From.GetSheHe] demands the heretic be burned before the rot spreads.
Build the pyre.
A difference of doctrine is no cause for burning.
My Lord Spiritual, [From.GetTitledFirstName], demands that [target_heretic.GetTitledName] and [target_heretic.GetHerHis] heresies be cast out of my court and my realm.
Let the heretic go, and never return.
No. [target_heretic.GetFirstName] stays.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] heeded me. The heretic [target_heretic.GetFirstName] burned, and the heresy with [target_heretic.GetHerHim].
The faith is cleansed.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] refused me. The heretic [target_heretic.GetFirstName] goes on spreading poison at court.
The gods will judge us all.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] heeded me. The heretic [target_heretic.GetFirstName] has been driven from the realm.
Good riddance.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] refused me. The heretic [target_heretic.GetFirstName] remains at court.
The gods will judge us all.

My steward [council_steward.GetTitledFirstName] collects my dues as the whim takes [council_steward.GetHerHim]: double the toll one week, a new tax on salt the next, a village fined for a quarrel no one remembers. The coin flows in, but so do the complaints.
Coin is coin.
Rein the steward in.
My steward [council_steward.GetTitledFirstName] has a name among the peasants as a fair and honest collector who weighs every claim and hears every plea. Even the tax is paid with less grumbling.
Fair dealing breeds loyal subjects.

Sickness has come to my lands. My steward [council_steward.GetTitledFirstName] has opened the granaries, hired every physician and herb-wife who would come, and paid for clean water to be carried to the worst-struck villages from [council_steward.GetHerHis] own budget.
Mercy has its uses.

My steward [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has a new way to collect my dues: anyone who cannot pay is flogged in the square, and the next village pays at once. It works, I cannot deny it. The tithe is double what it was.
Results are results.
Enough. This stops now.
[council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] is ordered to stop.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has forbidden my methods. Now the peasants will laugh in my face and pay nothing. Mark my words.
Weakness!

My diligent steward [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has followed the missing coin to its source: a thieves' guild operating openly in [council_thieves_province.GetName], with fences in every tavern and a bribed watch. The steward knows their names and their haunts. The guild can be rooted out, at a price, or quietly paid to move its business to someone else's lands.
Hang them all.
Pay them to take their trade elsewhere.
Every town has its thieves.

My steward [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has drawn up plans for my capital: new market halls, standard weights and measures, a toll bridge and a granary. It would cost me, but the steward swears the town would grow rich within a few years.
Do it.
Not now.

The robbers, smugglers and thieves in [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s lands pay a share to whoever looks away, and as steward I am well placed to do so. A few changed figures in the ledgers and no one would ever know.
Take a fat share.
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] may find out.
Take a little, no more.
The ledgers do not add up. My steward, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been taking money from the thieves and smugglers in my lands, and taking it from my own coffers too.
To the dungeon!
Every coin will be paid back.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] found out about my little arrangement. I am in the dungeon now.
Curses.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] found out about my little arrangement and made me pay back every coin.
At least I keep my head.

Something is wrong with my accounts. The tithes come in, the tolls come in, and yet my coffers never seem to fill. My steward [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has acquired a new house, a new horse and a fur cloak that would shame a Prince.
Summon the steward.
[council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] must answer for the accounts.
I am sure there is an explanation.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has summoned me and wants to know where the money went. My liege has the ledgers on the table and a very cold look.
Deny everything.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] may believe you.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] learns the truth.
Confess.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] walked me through the ledgers line by line: a flood here, a bad harvest there, a bridge rebuilt. It all adds up after all. I was wrong to suspect my steward.
My apologies, steward.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been stealing from me. The proof is plain: the house, the horse, the furs, all paid for from my coffers.
The thief will pay a heavy fine.
To the dungeon!
Let it pass, this once.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has fined me for my thefts and taken my purse. The fur cloak too.
Perhaps it is a lesson.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has thrown me in the dungeon for my thefts. There is little to spend money on down here.
Perhaps it is a lesson.

A band of kyazak has been roaming freely in one of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s oblasts, raiding stanitsas and burning the grain. I am itching to do something about it. I should ask [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] to let me ride out against them.

A band of highway robbers has been plaguing one of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s counties, robbing merchants and pilgrims on the roads and vanishing into the forest. I am itching to do something about it. I should ask [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] to let me ride out against them.
A rota of lancers would make short work of them!
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] is asked for soldiers to hunt the robbers.
A troop of soldiers would make short work of them!
It is not my concern.
The kyazak grow bolder by the week, burning more stanitsas and driving off the herds. Rotamaster [From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked to lead a rota against them personally and rid the oblast of them.
The robbers in my lands grow bolder by the week, and the merchants have begun to avoid my roads. Marshal [From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked to lead a force against them personally.
Take a full company, and do it properly.
Take the household guard and be quick about it.
Leave the robbers be.

I was a guest in the house of [council_wronged_patrician.GetTitledName] and drank too much. The daughter of the house mocked me at table and I struck her, harder than I meant. Her father will not let this pass. Soon [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] will hear of it.
She should have held her tongue.
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] hears of what you did.

[council_wronged_patrician.GetTitledName], one of my most prominent subjects, has come to me for justice. While Marshal [From.GetTitledFirstName] was a guest in [council_wronged_patrician.GetHerHis] house, the marshal beat [council_wronged_patrician.GetHerHis] daughter in a drunken rage. [council_wronged_patrician.GetSheHe] wants the marshal punished.
The marshal will pay compensation.
Into the dungeon with the marshal!
I will not punish my marshal for a drunken slap.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] is relieved.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has fined me and paid the money to that patrician's family. All for one slap.
Outrageous!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has thrown me in the dungeon, for one slap at a merchant's daughter. Is this how my years of service are repaid?
I will remember this.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent the patrician away with nothing. My liege knows the worth of a good marshal.
I am grateful, my liege.

Marshal [council_officer.GetTitledFirstName] has walked every wall and gate of my capital and drawn up plans: a new barbican, wider streets for the troops, a proper armoury and drill yard. It will cost me, but the marshal swears the town will be safer and richer for it.
Do it.
Not now.
